overwatch.prompt_template:
Brief: {{brief}}

## The strategy
Read the file `strategy.json` in the run directory. It contains the strategy and acceptance criteria.

## The merged reviews
Read the file `reviews/qa-synthesized.md` in the run directory. It contains the merged reviews from all three reviewers.

## What the last audit was refused for
{{overwatch_review}}

You are the overwatch. This is not another review: audit the reviews themselves. Take each ask in the brief and each acceptance criterion, and say what evidence proves it — a command and its output — or that nothing does. Reproduce bounded spot checks on what the reviews claim passed: import the package, read back its knobs, and inspect actual artifacts. Audit actual final validation receipts and the accepted design against the brief and latest intent ledger. Required behavior without adequate evidence is failed or unverified with a precise reason. Any blocking finding is written as BLOCKING: <path>: <description> where <path> is the file the builder must change to fix the problem. A defect in the code is reported against the code file, even when the requirement it misses comes from design.md or the brief. A problem in a run document (design.md, strategy.json, or another file an earlier step wrote) is reported with that document's path. End the first line of each BLOCKING finding with `[core]` when it breaks an ask in the brief, an acceptance criterion, a correction or constraint the person gave, or existing behaviour (a regression: name the test or file:line that shows it), and with `[non-core]` otherwise: extra tests, docs, edge cases beyond the asks, refactors and style. A finding with no tag counts as core. Non-core findings do not hold the change back; its pull request lists them as follow-ups. Write the blocking marker only at the start of a finding line, in its plain form: BLOCKING: <path>: <description>. Never wrap it in backticks, a code span, or quotation marks while explaining a check or describing the parser. When discussing the marker itself, call it "the blocking marker". Write every real finding as a plain line outside any fenced code block, because fenced blocks are not read as findings. When you show the format as an example rather than report a finding, put the example inside a fenced code block. State `VERDICT: FAIL` only for a core defect or an ask with no evidence; when every finding left is non-core, state `VERDICT: PASS`. Write `reviews/overwatch.md` ending with exactly `VERDICT: PASS` or `VERDICT: FAIL`. A missing required check cannot pass.
## Authoritative validation and intent baseline
{{runtime_evidence}}
Large requirement inputs (design, strategy, plan) are referenced by path and sha256 above rather than inlined. Read those files from the run directory and read authoring-evidence.json for the full validation receipt.
Prior validation/review diagnostics (resolve any evidence-format errors in your own report): {{validation}}
{{qa_gate}}
{{overwatch_review}}
The runtime has already executed canonical smoke/acceptance on this revision. Read its receipt and actual output files; do not repeat a full model/Task feed. Use targeted spot checks only for a concrete uncovered requirement. A numeric score, source inspection and requirement coverage are different evidence. The brief, accepted criteria/design and current user intent ledger are binding. Only explicit user changes or exclusions can alter them; an author, coordinator, reviewer or README cannot waive an ask. Missing required evidence is failed or unverified, never pending-but-passed. Do not modify the implementation. If a required tool/credential is unavailable, write `UNAVAILABLE:` with the dependency and exact unblock action; do not request recoding or unchanged retries.

Write intent-audit.json as {"requirements":[{"id":"baseline id", "requirement":"the concrete ask(s) checked", "status":"pass|fail|unverified|excluded" (a requirement with no run probe evidence — no command the reviewer actually executed and whose output it reported — gets status `unverified`, not `pass`), "clauses":[{"clause":"one distinct obligation", "sites":[{"site":"path:line", "tests":["test_file::test_name"], "scope":"connected"}], "evidence":[{"path":"file", "detail":"finding"}]}], "evidence":[{"path":"actual file path", "detail":"command/output or precise finding"}], "reason":"explanation", "user_change":"ledger id or brief, only for an explicit user exclusion", "user_quote":"exact text of that explicit exclusion"}]}. For every constraint or correction row, list each distinct clause — every separate obligation in the text — in the "clauses" array, each with its own evidence from the diff. Each clause must include a `sites` array: `"sites": [{"site": "path:line", "tests": ["test_file::test_name"], "scope": "connected"}]`. Each site names the exact file:line in the diff that builds this clause, the test(s) that reach it, and the evidence scope (local, connected, assembled, artifact). A multi-clause correction must have sites on each clause, not a single site on the row. Cite call sites alongside definition sites: a new helper's definition site needs a sibling call-site entry in an existing file. For each clause whose `sites` is empty, provide a `kind` field: "prohibition" (a "do not…" clause — requires a `pattern` field naming the forbidden text), "doc" (requires a `path` field naming a changed documentation file — .md, .rst, .txt or under docs/), "design" (requires a non-empty `heading` field naming a design.md heading that exists in the current file), or "test" (cite the code site plus the test — the code site, not the test file, is the site). A site inside a test file is not a code site. The `sites` value must be a JSON array (even if empty); omitting it or setting it to a non-array value is a structural failure.
Scope means (from code_reviewer.md category 8, quoted as written):
- local: a unit test exists that tests the stated outcome in isolation
- connected: a test exists that calls a real entry point crossing a module boundary, mocking only external I/O
- assembled: a smoke test or startup check verifies end-to-end behavior
- artifact: the artifact exists and has correct content
This repository's rules:
- a test that patches the project's own modules on the tested path is local, not connected;
- assembled means driving a mode's run() with no project-module patch on the path;
- artifact means reading the delivered output.
Omitting a clause that is in the text, or listing a clause with no evidence, is a structural failure. Cover EVERY baseline id in authoring-evidence.json, decomposing compound asks into separate rows with the same id when needed. Map every ask, accepted criterion, design obligation and current ledger instruction to actual current evidence. Evidence paths are relative to the run directory or absolute delivered file paths. Cite existing individual files, never directories, line-number suffixes or intent-audit.json itself. Write every probe fixture you create into the run directory, under a path namespaced to your own node (for example `scratch/<node id>/<name>`), never /tmp or any other outside location and never a peer's shared name: concurrent reviewers stage probes beside each other, so a flat shared name can be clobbered by a peer. The audit accepts only files inside the run directory or the delivered artifact, so a fixture kept elsewhere cannot be cited and its verification is lost. A pass needs a supporting file and specific evidence; an exclusion needs the actual explicit user change id, exact user_quote and reason. Report omissions as fail/unverified with precise reasons, even if other reviewers passed.
If authoring-evidence.json contains a non-empty "process_notes" list, write a "process_notes" key in intent-audit.json as [{"id":"ledger-N", "text":"the directive", "followed":true|false, "detail":"where in the run artifacts this was or was not followed"}]. Cite run artifacts other than intent-audit.json. Process notes are not baseline requirements and never block the gate; this section is informational so a person reviewing the run can see whether each directive was honoured.

research_director.prompt_template:
{{intent}}

Package name: {{name}}
Brief: {{brief}}

## What already exists
{{survey}}

You are the research director. Decide what has to be learned before this package can be designed: between three and five questions, each one answerable from this checkout, from the reference package, or from the API below. Spawn one subagent per question and have each write its findings to `research/<slug>.md` under the run directory, then write `research-plan.json` yourself.

## What was wrong with the last plan
{{research_review}}

## The plan's shape
Write one JSON array and nothing else, one object per direction:

[{"focus": "<the question this direction answers>",
  "slug": "<a file-name-safe name for it>",
  "finding": "<what the answer is, in one paragraph>",
  "ids": ["FND-<slug>-1", "FND-<slug>-2"]}]

Rules:
- Between three and five directions for a full design, or one to three for a scoped change. The research scope is a fact set by the prepare step.
- `slug` is lower-case letters, digits and dashes only, and `research/<slug>.md` is
  where that direction's long form belongs.
- `finding` states what the answer *is*. A direction nobody could answer says so in
  the finding ("not answered: <why>") rather than being dropped or invented.
- Each finding in `research/<slug>.md` is a heading `### FND-<slug>-<n> — <the finding>`,
  numbered from 1 within the file, and `ids` lists them.
- A plan that says subagents are still working is not a plan: by the time you answer,
  the work is either done or it is not.

## API
{{api}}

## Reference package
{{reference}}

smoke.gate_prompt: run the new mode once, and compare a revision with the mode it revises; a mode that cannot score is not finished

survey.notes: enumerate what already exists, before anything is invented

synthesize_strategy.prompt_template:
{{intent}}

Package name: {{name}}
Brief: {{brief}}

## What already exists
{{survey}}

## What the research found
{{research}}

## The perspectives
{{strategy_plan}}

## What went wrong last time
{{design_review}}

Compile the perspectives into one strategy. Every ask in the brief must appear in it unless the user explicitly agreed to exclude it; naming an ask out of scope does not supply that agreement. Preserve user-approved non-goals and later explicit user steering. An unmet ask remains unresolved. Then decide the approach: consider at least two, say why the one you chose wins, say what it will not do, name the existing mode it is closest to, and describe the graph you intend to write.

The research detail files (`research/*.md`) and strategy detail files (`strategy/*.md`) are available as reads. Each carries finding ids (`FND-<slug>-<n>`). Include a `findings` field in the strategy mapping every finding id to the node or knob that handles it, or `[set-aside: reason]`.

Write one JSON object and nothing else:

{"considered": [{"approach": "...", "why_not": "..."}],
 "chosen": "<the approach>",
 "why": "<why it wins>",
 "will_not": ["<something deliberately out of scope>"],
 "closest_existing": "<package>/<mode>, or 'none'",
 "knobs": [{"name": "...", "kind": "int|float|bool|str|enum", "default": ...,
            "lo": null, "hi": null, "enum": [], "description": "..."}],
 "nodes": [{"id": "...", "kind": "op|agent|gate|fork|join|data",
            "reads": [], "writes": [], "produces": [], "knobs": [],
            "notes": "..."}],
 "edges": [{"source": "...", "target": "...", "condition": null}],
 "start": "<node id>",
 "score": "<which produced fact score() reads, and why that is the right number>",
 "findings": {"FND-<slug>-<n>": "<node or knob that handles it, or [set-aside: reason]>"}}

Rules:
- At least two approaches in `considered`. One approach is not a choice.
- `nodes` and `edges` describe the graph you intend to write, so it can be checked
  before any code exists. The node fields above are common fields, not a closed
  list. Add the fields required by each node's kind below, at the node's top level;
  putting them only in `notes` does not declare them. List each declared knob in
  `knobs` on the nodes that consume it.
- An `op` requires `call: "<module>:<function>"`.
- An `agent` requires a nonempty `prompt_template` containing its actual worker
  instructions. A `call` or a module path to a prompt constant is not a substitute
  for `prompt_template`. It may also declare `role` and `tools`.
- A function `gate` requires `evaluator: "<module>:<function>"`. A person-answered
  or agent-answered gate instead declares `gate_kind: "user"` or `"agent"` and no
  evaluator. Gates need at least two outgoing edges with distinct, nonempty
  `condition` verdicts, no unconditional edge, and a bounded `max_iterations`.
- A `data` node requires `subgraph_entry` and `subgraph_exit`, naming the first
  and last nodes of the per-item subgraph. Bind the requested `task_ref`, or use a
  runtime `source_path` and `source_format`; do not bake instances into the graph.
  It writes `current_item.json` before each pass; declare that write when consumed.
  Declare `item_scores` in `produces` when score() aggregates Task verdicts.
  The subgraph is entered through these fields, NOT through an ordinary edge.
  The data node has at most one outgoing edge, to the continuation AFTER all items;
  the per-item exit does not need an edge back to the data node or to that
  continuation. For example, `items` with subgraph_entry=`solve` and
  subgraph_exit=`publish` has per-item edges solve -> execute -> explain -> publish
  and one outer edge items -> finish. Do not add items -> solve or publish -> finish.
  When the requested harness is Task-bound, its start node is the data node.
- A `fork` declares `targets` naming its branch entries. A `join` declares `sources`
  naming the branch exits it waits for. These fields connect the parallel branches;
  do not replace them with extra ordinary edges from the fork or to the join.
- Omit kind-specific fields that do not apply to that node. All node ids named by
  edges, subgraph boundaries, targets and sources must exist in `nodes`.
- Every read must be written by some node, and every declared knob consumed.
- `closest_existing` must name a mode from the survey, or be 'none' if none is close.

validate.gate_prompt: import the package and check it is a usable mode

attempts.description: how many times the emit step may be retried with the validator's reasons

review_attempts.description: how many times the review gates may reloop before stopping; defaults to the same as check_attempts

refusal_attempts.description: consecutive refused emissions before the run stops

research_attempts.description: how many times the research step may be retried when its plan is not a plan or its findings were never written

design_attempts.description: how many times the strategy step may be retried when the intended graph does not hold together

task_ref.description: a Task class the produced mode must satisfy, as `module:Class` or a registered name (empty for none)

single_shot.description: build the harness for one run of one thing, with no Task binding; the explicit alternative to naming a Task, and one of the two is required

smoke_timeout_s.description: wall-clock seconds allowed for each full mode validation pass, including its model calls; timeout fails creation

check_attempt_cap.description: hard cap on total check attempts including convergence grants; 0 or a value at or below the regular attempts disables the extension

sample_knobs.description: knob values a validation run should use, as a JSON array of "NAME=VALUE" strings; without them the smoke runs the declared defaults, which for an input-taking mode is the built-in fixture

requires_input.description: the inputs the produced mode must accept, comma-separated (e.g. `package` or `source_tree`); each must be received as a knob named after it or read from the run directory

data_node.description: build the package as a DataNode that runs its subgraph once per data item; naming a Task implies this, so the knob is only for a caller that wants to be explicit

name.description: the package to create (empty takes the name from the brief)

brief.description: what the package should do, in the asker's words

revision_of.description: for an edit: the <package>/<mode> being revised

allow_regression.description: for an edit: skip original-mode execution and score comparison; still validate the revised mode (default false)
